title: Common Dependency Injection Problems knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Common Dependency Injection Problems”?
options: Common Dependency Injection Problems should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Common Dependency Injection Problems helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Common Dependency Injection Problems means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Common Dependency Injection Problems removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Common Dependency Injection Problems helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Common Dependency Injection Problems is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Missing provider errors” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Missing provider errors” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Missing provider errors” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.

questions.answer_key: Connect “Missing provider errors” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Missing provider errors” under Common Dependency Injection Problems. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Common Dependency Injection Problems”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
